discoveredAssets: GET /login - Public login page with HTML form returning user to /add_prescription on success
POST /graphql - GraphQL API endpoint with full introspection enabled (no authentication required for schema queries)
GET /view_prescriptions - Protected prescription retrieval endpoint requiring authentication (returns 401)
GET /logout - Protected session termination endpoint requiring authentication (returns 401)

targets.objective: Test GraphQL API for authorization flaws (query/mutation access without authentication), IDOR via userId parameter manipulation, NoSQL/GraphQL injection in addPrescription mutation, field disclosure in queries, and schema-level vulnerabilities
targets.rationale: GraphQL introspection enabled without authentication - full schema exposed. getPrescriptions query and addPrescription mutation allow userId manipulation which could lead to cross-user data access. 'flag' field in PrescriptionType suggests sensitive data exposure risk.

targets.objective: Test authentication endpoint for SQL/NoSQL injection in username/password fields, default credentials, credential enumeration, brute force resistance, session management flaws, and JWT/token vulnerabilities
targets.rationale: Authentication is the primary attack surface. POST /login accepts JSON with username/password. Successful login stores userID in localStorage. Need to test for authentication bypass and weak session management.

targets.objective: Test protected endpoint for authorization bypasses, IDOR accessing other users' data, injection in prescription details, CSRF attacks, and business logic flaws once authenticated
targets.rationale: Protected endpoint after login. Critical prescription management functionality. Risk of data modification for other users or parameter tampering. Need to test authorization between users.

targets.objective: Test endpoint for horizontal privilege escalation (accessing other users' prescriptions via userId manipulation), data disclosure, and improper authorization checks
targets.rationale: Prescription retrieval endpoint likely vulnerable to IDOR attacks. userId parameter shown in GraphQL schema suggests manual user ID manipulation could retrieve other users' prescriptions.

targets.objective: Test logout functionality for session fixation, incomplete session termination, and improper credential handling
targets.rationale: Session management endpoint requiring authentication. Test that logout properly terminates sessions and prevents token reuse.

keyFindings: [CRITICAL] GraphQL introspection fully enabled without authentication - Complete schema exposed including Query types (getPrescriptions), Mutations (addPrescription), and field types
[CRITICAL] GraphQL mutations potentially callable without authentication - addPrescription mutation accepts userId and prescriptionDetails parameters
[HIGH] userId parameter in GraphQL queries/mutations suggests potential IDOR vulnerability - Different user IDs could retrieve/modify other users' prescriptions
[HIGH] localStorage usage for userID - Client-side authentication token storage vulnerable to XSS attacks
[HIGH] Flag field in PrescriptionType schema - Indicates presence of sensitive data that may be exfiltrated through information disclosure
[HIGH] POST /login endpoint accepts JSON credentials without visible rate limiting - Potential for credential brute force attacks
[MEDIUM] No rate limiting visible on GraphQL endpoint - Could allow rapid query/mutation execution
[MEDIUM] Application uses Python/Werkzeug framework - Standard Flask security issues may apply
[MEDIUM] No security headers visible (X-Frame-Options, CSP, HSTS) - Potential for clickjacking and other header-based attacks
